title: FAC-SEM-012 refuses every Windows command path, including the repository's own positive task-scheduler fixture
source: src/semantic-rules.ts:106-111 (serviceCommands regex /^(~\/|\/)/); fixtures/positive/service-descriptor-task-scheduler.json commands.doctor[0] = "C:\\Users\\example\\...\\example-agent.exe"; docs/specification/service.md:70 ("Paths MAY start with `~/`") and :527 ("absolute or `~/` executable path"); DEC-0032 (docs/DECISIONS.md:1016 'localPath accepts drive-absolute (C:\…, C:/…) and ~\ paths')
evidence: Probe in the mutation copy: evaluateSemanticRules('service-descriptor', <positive/service-descriptor-task-scheduler.json>) -> [{"code":"FAC-SEM-012","instancePath":"/commands/doctor/0","message":"command doctor must start with an absolute or home-relative executable path"}]; same for doctor[0] = "~\\bin\\x.exe". No test runs semantic rules over positive service-descriptor fixtures, so the suite stays green (test/service-rules.test.ts only uses POSIX descriptors).
proposed_fix: Accept drive-absolute (`[A-Za-z]:[\\/]`) and `~\` executables in FAC-SEM-012 (same grammar as service-common localPath), keep refusing bare names and UNC; update service.md:70 and the FAC-SEM-012 row at :527 to name the Windows forms; add a test that runs evaluateSemanticRules over every positive service-descriptor fixture (and a Windows bare-name negative).

title: service.md Lifecycle still macOS-only for Install, Code, State and Uninstall after DEC-0032 added systemd and Task Scheduler
source: docs/specification/service.md:367 (Install: 'Write the plist, bootout … bootstrap'), :370 (Code: 'An upgrade rewrites the plist'), :371 (State: data/logs/cache only under ~/Library/...), :372 (Uninstall: 'bootout, delete the plist'), :365 (One copy: 'service.lock in its data directory'); DEC-0032 docs/DECISIONS.md:1013-1015 ('Start, stop, restart and state per system are in service.md Lifecycle (Off)')
evidence: Only the Supervisor (:366) and Off (:369) rows were made per-system. A Linux or Windows writer has no contract for install/upgrade/uninstall (unit write + daemon-reload/enable, schtasks create/delete) or for where data, logs and cache live. The adapter already defines Linux directories the contract lacks: fabric-agent-adapter/plugins/fabric-agent-adapter/skills/building-fabric-services/references/lifecycle.md:84-90 (XDG_DATA_HOME/XDG_STATE_HOME/XDG_CACHE_HOME), and nothing for Windows.
needs: A decision record (contract maintainers with the Fabric Dashboards FD-37 and Fabric CO-238 sessions, as DEC-0032 was agreed) fixing the Linux and Windows data/log/cache locations and the install/upgrade/uninstall steps per supervisor.
proposed_fix: Add per-system columns to Install, Code, State and Uninstall: systemd (write ~/.config/systemd/user/<unit>, daemon-reload, enable --now; uninstall disable --now, remove unit, daemon-reload), Task Scheduler (create/delete the per-user task); State: XDG dirs on Linux (as the adapter already uses), %LOCALAPPDATA%\<id>\ on Windows; DEC entry plus mermaid at :40 naming all three supervisors.

title: localPath accepts a forward-slash UNC path (//server/share) although 'a network share is never a local path'
source: schemas/service-common.schema.json:19 pattern ^(~[\\/]|/|[A-Za-z]:[\\/])...; :21 description 'Never a network share'; service.md:358-359; fixtures/negative/service-descriptor-unc-token.json (backslash form only)
evidence: Probe: positive task-scheduler descriptor with auth.tokenFile='//server/share/service.token' -> {"valid":true,"errors":[]}; '\\\\?\\C:\\x\\token' -> false. Windows treats //server/share as UNC, so a Windows host opening that token file reaches the network (SMB auth).
proposed_fix: Change the POSIX alternative to '/(?![/\\])' (refuse a leading // or /\) and add a negative fixture service-descriptor-unc-forward-slash; note in service.md:358 that //server/... is a share too.

title: CT-01 still undecided; DEC-0032 widened it from launchd to every supervisor
source: docs/backlog.md:12 (CT-01 open since 71cdd6e, 2026-10-04); docs/specification/service.md:365 (One copy: lock held -> MUST print one sentence and exit 75) and :366 (launchd KeepAlive true/ThrottleInterval 10; systemd Restart=always/RestartSec=10; Task Scheduler restart on failure every minute); fabric-agent-adapter .../building-fabric-services/references/lifecycle.md:73-80 (supervised copy backs off 0.5 s doubling to 30 s, 300 s total, exits 75 when the wait runs out, keyed on FABRIC_SERVICE_SUPERVISOR=launchd)
evidence: grep -n 'service.lock\|exit 75\|status 75\|FABRIC_SERVICE_SUPERVISOR' docs src schemas -> only service.md:365 and backlog.md:12; no DEC after DEC-0031 touches the rule (DEC-0032..0040 read). Under systemd Restart=always/RestartSec=10 an immediate exit 75 loops every 10 s exactly as under launchd; under Task Scheduler the restart count is finite, so repeated exit 75 can leave the task stopped. The adapter's back-off is launchd-only and its signal variable is not in the contract.
needs: A DEC (reserve with agent_sync.py reserve DEC) agreed by the contract maintainers with the adapter and Fabric Dashboards sessions. Likely decision: keep 'MUST NOT perform a side effect without the lock' and 'exit 75 with one sentence naming the holder', and add 'a copy started by its supervisor MAY wait for the lock first, touching nothing, for at most 300 s (≥ the drain time), then exit 75; a copy started by hand exits at once'; name the signal in the contract (e.g. FABRIC_SERVICE_SUPERVISOR=<lifecycle.manager>, written by the writer into the plist/unit/task environment, never inferred from the parent process); state per supervisor that exit 75 is restarted (launchd, systemd) or consumes a finite restart count (Task Scheduler).
proposed_fix: Write the DEC above, amend the One copy row, add the env var to the Supervisor row for all three managers, close CT-01 with the DEC id and the adapter repin as receipt.

title: The appearance cookie is per host, not per origin: on 127.0.0.1 every local service shares one fabric_appearance
source: docs/specification/embedded-dashboard.md:74-77 (ED-8: 'set in the page's own storage partition on the service origin'), :130-131 (per-service choice 'not decided'); service.md:66 (every local origin is http://127.0.0.1:<port>)
evidence: RFC 6265 §8.5: 'Cookies do not provide isolation by port'. A cookie set for 127.0.0.1 is sent to every port, so every local dashboard reads (and any local page can overwrite) the same fabric_appearance; a per-service choice cannot be carried by this cookie for local placements, and 'on the service origin' is inaccurate.
proposed_fix: Reword ED-8 to say the cookie is scoped to the host and therefore shared by every local service on 127.0.0.1; add to 'Not decided here' that a per-service choice for local placements needs a different carrier (e.g. a per-service cookie name or a query/postMessage channel).

title: ED-6 requires every declared page to apply scheme and theme, while ED-9 'appearance' lets a page declare a subset or nothing
source: docs/specification/embedded-dashboard.md:58-63 (ED-6: when the cookie is present its values take precedence and the page MUST hide its own scheme and theme controls), :94 (ED-9: a page meeting ED-1…ED-6 SHOULD declare), :102 ('appearance' optional: any of scheme, theme), :90 (host MAY reload a page that does not declare appearance)
evidence: A page declaring appearance:['scheme'] meets ED-6 only if it also applies the theme, so the subset has no conformant meaning; a declaring page that omits 'appearance' is simultaneously claimed ED-6-conformant and treated as not applying the carrier (reload fallback).
needs: Contract maintainers with Fabric Dashboards (ED-8 owner): whether ED-6 binds each carrier field only when listed in 'appearance', or 'appearance' means 'applies without reload'.
proposed_fix: Either make ED-6 conditional on the fields listed in 'appearance' (and absent = scheme via prefers-color-scheme only), or redefine 'appearance' as live application (no reload needed) and say ED-6 always applies both fields.

title: An invalid dashboard declaration is accepted by the well-known schema, and the spec does not say what a host does with it
source: schemas/service-well-known.schema.json:306-307 (extensions -> common $defs, unconstrained); docs/specification/embedded-dashboard.md:94-109 (ED-9; host behaviour only for 'not declared'); src/ (no use of service-dashboard-extension outside tests: grep -rn dashboard src/*.ts)
evidence: Probe: service-well-known-dashboard fixture with the dashboard key set to {minWidth: 99999, zoom: 3} -> service-well-known valid true. A host computing max(480, minWidth) from it would give the page more than any window; nothing in the contract's checker flags it (the check lives only in the adapter's check_service.py).
needs: Contract maintainers with Fabric Dashboards: an invalid declaration is treated as a legacy dashboard (ignored) or as a nonconforming service.
proposed_fix: Add to ED-9: 'A host validates the value against the schema and treats an invalid one as not declared'; add a contract-side check (semantic kind service-well-known or a validateExtensions helper) and a negative semantic fixture.
